If both conditions are true, it throws an `IllegalStateException`. Otherwise, it proceeds to retrieve a single subscription from the `subscriptionsByJID` map. The Javadoc explicitly documents that this exception is thrown when the method is used in a context where multiple subscriptions are supported. The throw is a guard to prevent ambiguous results—since the method returns a single subscription by JID, it is only safe to call when either multiple subscriptions are disabled, or if enabled but there is at most one subscription per JID. The programmer intended this exception to signal a precondition violation, meaning the caller should either ensure the condition is not met (by checking beforehand) or be prepared to handle the exception if the condition occurs. The documented `@throws` clause in the Javadoc further indicates that the exception is an expected part of the method's contract, implying callers should be aware of it and likely catch it when they cannot guarantee the preconditions.
